chunks: (Say): "Then should I seek (the source of) law elsewhere than God, when it is He who has revealed this Book to you, which distinctly explains (everything)?" Those to whom We have given the Book know it has been sent by your Lord in truth. So be not a sceptic.
ai.seo_question: Who is the ultimate judge and source of the Quran according to Surah Al-An'am?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the concept of *Tawhid al-Tashri'* (Oneness of Legislation), asserting that divine law is exclusively from Allah, distinct from human or idolatrous sources. It highlights the consensus of the *Ahl al-Kitab* (People of the Book) regarding the Quran's divine origin, serving as a rational proof against doubt (*al-mumtari*). This reinforces the authority of the Quran as the detailed, unambiguous guide for all aspects of life.
